name: Arbëresh Albanian

allophone_rules.notes: Intervocalic ⟨g⟩ /ɡ/ lenites to the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] (Wikipedia: Arbëresh language). Expressed as a context rule rather than a blanket grapheme override so the plain plosive /ɡ/ survives word-finally, where AAE_DEVOICE_G still applies.
Archaic final-obstruent devoicing preserved from medieval Tosk, lost in the modern standard. Wikipedia (Arbëresh language): lig ('bad') is pronounced [lɪk].
Word-final devoicing of /d/, same archaic pattern as other voiced obstruents.
Word-final devoicing of /ɡ/; example cited on Wikipedia: lig ('bad') → [lɪk].
Word-final devoicing of the dental fricative dh /ð/ → [θ].

ancestors.notes: Arbëresh descends from medieval (Old) Tosk Albanian, carried to Italy by Albanian settlers from the 15th century onward; grapheme_base sq (Tosk-derived standard) approximates the shared Latin orthography, with local overrides.

Centuries of contact with Sicilian and (southern) Italian produced substantial lexical borrowing, e.g. qaca ('square') < Sicilian chiazza, pincar ('think') < Sicilian pinzari (Wikipedia: Arbëresh language).

notes: Arbëresh (Arbërisht), spoken by the Italo-Albanian (Arbëreshë) communities of Sicily and Calabria since the 15th-century diaspora. Preserves medieval Tosk features lost in the modern standard: no front rounded vowel /y/, so ⟨y⟩ merges with /i/; ⟨ll⟩ and intervocalic ⟨g⟩ are realized as the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] (a feature carried into local speakers' Italian, per Wikipedia); archaic word-final devoicing of voiced obstruents. First-person singular present indicative ends in ⟨-nj⟩ rather than standard ⟨-j⟩ (morphological, not encoded here). Earliest text: E Mbësuame e Krështerë (1592) by Lekë Matrënga.

location.notes: Approximate Arbëresh-speaking area, Calabria/Sicily, southern Italy.
